study type: Diagnostic Accuracy Study (with a case-control design)
exposure: Ultrasonic lung imaging diagnosis model based on a deep residual network (DRN) algorithm
Deep residual network (DRWSR) based on wavelet domain
Deep residual network detection with normalization framework (Fisher-DRN)
outcome: Diagnostic performance of AI algorithms (segmentation accuracy, image feature extraction accuracy, algorithm convergence, time loss, AUC area)
cohort: 90 premature infants in a hospital, divided into an experimental group (45 with NRDS) and a control group (45 without NRDS).
finding: The ultrasound lung imaging diagnosis model based on the DRN algorithm demonstrated superior diagnostic performance for NRDS compared to other algorithms (e.g., AUCs of 0.962, 0.881, and 0.902 for different grades), and infants with NRDS had significantly lower gestational age, birth weight, and Apgar scores.
cross-section timing: At the time of suspected or diagnosed NRDS in premature infants.
birth_weight: Measured; NRDS group had remarkably lower birth weight (P<0.05).
gest_age: Measured; NRDS group had remarkably lower gestational age (P<0.05).
